about:
# Profit

A WoW Forever addon to find the most profitable profession crafts, using Auctionator's
price data (`Auctionator.API.v1`) for materials and crafted items.

## Install (development)

Requires Auctionator. Link this repo into the client's AddOns folder; the link must be
named `Profit` to match `Profit.toc`:

```sh
ln -s "$PWD" "/Applications/World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/Profit"
```

The minimap button uses LibDBIcon. Releases bundle it, but `Libs/` isn't committed, so a linked
copy needs the libraries fetched once (the same ones `.pkgmeta` lists):

```sh
W=https://repos.wowace.com/wow
mkdir -p Libs/LibStub Libs/CallbackHandler-1.0 Libs/LibDataBroker-1.1 Libs/LibDBIcon-1.0
curl -so Libs/LibStub/LibStub.lua $W/libstub/trunk/LibStub.lua
curl -so Libs/CallbackHandler-1.0/CallbackHandler-1.0.lua $W/callbackhandler/trunk/CallbackHandler-1.0/CallbackHandler-1.0.lua
curl -so Libs/LibDataBroker-1.1/LibDataBroker-1.1.lua https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tekkub/libdatabroker-1-1/master/LibDataBroker-1.1.lua
for f in LibDBIcon-1.0.lua lib.xml; do curl -so Libs/LibDBIcon-1.0/$f $W/libdbicon-1-0/trunk/LibDBIcon-1.0/$f; done
```

In game, after an Auctionator scan:

- `/prof`: opens the window. Dropdowns pick the filter (Known only, the default / Known +
  trainable, which leaves out recipes only learned from patterns / Known + learnable / All
  recipes) and the profession (all, your main professions, i.e. the primary
  ones you have, or one profession); click a column to sort and a recipe for its breakdown;
  clicking a recipe you know also opens it in your profession window. The Skill column shows
  where an unlearned recipe comes from (trainer, pattern or both) and the skill to learn it.
  Recipe names are colored by skill-up chance at your skill; grey recipes are listed too,
  since they can still be profitable. The Disenchant column is the profit from disenchanting
  the crafted item instead of selling it, using the expected value of its materials.
  Enchanters also get **Disenchant from AH**: gear Auctionator has priced that's worth more
  disenchanted than it costs, leaving out items above your Enchanting skill. Clicking an item
  with the auction house open searches for it through Auctionator.
- `/prof top [count] [profession]`: most profitable known or learnable crafts, in chat
- `/prof <recipe name>`: learn level, cost, sale value after the auction house cut, vendor value, profit,
  and for green or better gear what it disenchants into and the disenchant profit
- `/prof export`: a string of your trainer, merchant and disenchant recordings to copy and share
- `/prof minimap`: show or hide the minimap button (click it to open the window, drag to move it)
- `/prof tooltip`: show or hide the estimated disenchant value and craft cost in item tooltips (on
  by default; hold Shift for the disenchant materials and their chances, and the craft's reagents
  and profit). The craft cost uses the cheapest recipe you know, or the cheapest of any if you know none.
- `/prof changelog`: what's new in each update (also shown once after updating)
- `/prof debug`: the client build, which game API each feature uses (MISSING if one is missing),
  and what's been detected and recorded; paste it into bug reports

Vendor-sold materials are priced at their vendor price; everything else uses Auctionator.
The addon reads your profession skills from your skill list, and which recipes you know
each time you open a profession window.

## Recipe data

`export/recipes.json` (and the addon's `Data/*.lua`) is generated from the WoW Forever client's DB2 tables, downloaded as CSV
from [wago.tools](https://wago.tools/). Regenerate it after each new client build:

```sh
python3 tools/build_recipes.py            # latest Forever build on wago.tools
python3 tools/build_recipes.py --build 1.60.1.70124
```

Tables are cached in `tools/.cache/<build>/`; pass `--refresh` to re-download.

Server hotfixes (Blizzard's hotfix posts) don't reach the tables until a later build, so
`tools/hotfixes.py` keeps them by hand and the build applies them. The build says when the
client data has caught up, so the entry can be removed.

Each recipe records what it makes (and how many), its materials, required tools and
crafting station, its skill-up range, and `sources`: every way to learn it. A recipe can
have several (e.g. `["trainer", "item"]`: taught by a trainer, or learned from a pattern
bought at the auction house).

| Source | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `trainer` | Seen at a trainer in game (see below) or listed by Zockify, with the skill needed to learn it when known; also recipes learned automatically with the profession (skill 1) |
| `item` | Taught by a recipe item (listed in `recipe_items`, with the skill needed to learn it) |
| `drop`, `vendor`, `quest` | From Zockify (below), for recipes with no recipe item in the client data and no trainer |
| `trainer_inferred` | Only when nothing else applies: no recipe item exists, so probably a trainer; could also be a quest or special source |
| `unknown` | Only when nothing else applies: the client data looks incomplete (see `issues`); likely not obtainable in Forever |

Where recipes are learned comes from [Zockify](https://www.zockify.com/forever/)'s recipe tables
(`tools/zockify.py`, cached in `tools/.cache/zockify/`; `--refresh` re-downloads them, `--no-zockify`
leaves them out). Rows are matched by profession and recipe (or product) name. Each matched recipe
gets `zockify`: Zockify's source kinds and its `where` lines (drops, vendors, quests), which the
addon shows in recipe details. Zockify only replaces `trainer_inferred` and `unknown` sources, and
patterns it says a vendor sells for gold are marked as limited vendor stock. In-game recordings
still take priority.

The client data does not include trainer skill requirements, which vendors stock an item,
or drop sources. Those fields are `null` rather than guessed, until filled in by recordings.

Items record their disenchant bracket (`disenchant`), from the client's `ItemDisenchantLoot`
table (item class, quality, item level) and its no-disenchant item flag. What each bracket
yields is a server loot table, not in the client data, so `tools/disenchant.py` keeps the
Classic results by hand, along with the Enchanting skill each bracket needs (unknown for epics
below item level 61). The top-level `disenchant` maps each bracket to its item class,
quality and item level range, its `results`, and the items in the client data in that bracket;
`no_disenchant` lists gear flagged as not disenchantable. The client data lacks many items (the
server sends them), so in game the addon matches those to a bracket from `GetItemInfo`.

## Recording trainers and merchants

The addon records into its saved variables (`ProfitDB`) whenever a window opens:

- **Trainers**: the skill needed to learn each recipe, including ones already known or not
  yet available.
- **Merchants**: items sold for gold, and whether stock is limited (usually recipe items).
- **Disenchants**: what each disenchanted item gave (counts per material). If a result isn't
  in `tools/disenchant.py`'s table for that item, or the item wasn't expected to disenchant,
  a popup asks the player to share their `/prof export`. The importer prints these as
  `unexpected:` lines; fix `tools/disenchant.py` (or the bracket data) to match.
  `/prof testdisenchant` makes the next disenchant show the popup, to try it out.

Vendor materials start from the hand-kept list in `tools/vendor_items.txt`. To ship what
you've recorded, log out (so WoW writes the saved variables), then:

```sh
python3 tools/import_recorded.py   # merges WTF/Account/*/SavedVariables/Profit.lua into export/recorded.json
python3 tools/build_recipes.py
```

Strings other players send from `/prof export` import the same way: save them to a text
file (one per line) and run `python3 tools/import_recorded.py strings.txt`.

Commit `export/recorded.json` with the regenerated data.

# Profit

## [v0.3.4](https://github.com/ExcEssIv3/profit/tree/v0.3.4) (2026-11-17)

- Craft costs in item tooltips

    recipe (or the cheapest of any, marked "not known"). Shift shows the

# Profit

## [v0.3.3](https://github.com/ExcEssIv3/profit/tree/v0.3.3) (2026-11-11)

- Recipe sources from Zockify, client build 70888 and November hotfixes  
    - tools/zockify.py scrapes Zockify's WoW Forever recipe tables; the build matches  
      them by name to confirm trainer recipes (with learn levels), mark drop/quest/vendor  
      sources, flag vendor-sold patterns and add where-to-learn text shown in details.  
    - tools/hotfixes.py holds server hotfixes the client tables don't have yet.  
    - Data regenerated from client build 1.60.1.70888; import\_recorded.py reads the  
      live client's WTF folder and merges new merchant recordings.

# Profit

[Full Changelog](https://github.com/ExcEssIv3/profit/commits/v0.3.2) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/ExcEssIv3/profit/releases)

- LibDBIcon minimap button and data for the live client (build 70790)

    - Sell dropdown (AH, Vendor, Highest): revenue and profit for the chosen buyer; Highest marks  
      vendor prices with "(vendor)".  
    - Materials the character can craft are priced at their crafting cost when that's cheaper,  
      down any chain of crafts; recipe details show what they're crafted from.  
    - Favorites per character: a star column (shown on hover, click to toggle), right-click or the  
      Favorite button, and a Favorites filter at the top of the dropdown.

    Closes #6, closes #7, closes #8.

    the package.

- Disenchanting: values, AH deals, tooltips and recording

      Enchanting skill kept by hand in tools/disenchant.py; Data/Disenchant.lua covers every  
      disenchantable item, and items the client data lacks are matched in game via GetItemInfo  
    - Disenchant column and recipe breakdown: profit from crafting to disenchant  
    - Item tooltips show the expected disenchant value (Shift for materials); /prof tooltip  
    - "Disenchant from AH" filter for enchanters: gear priced by Auctionator worth more  
      disenchanted than it costs; clicking searches the auction house  
    - Record disenchant results, popup on unexpected ones, include them in /prof export and  
      the importer; /prof testdisenchant  
    - /prof debug opens a copyable window with the addon version  
    - Profit column fits its values; header left-aligned  
    - Import player recordings (51 merchant items); data for client build 70245  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- What's new popup, Blacksmithing and Mining trainer data  
    - Changelog.lua: release notes shown once after an update (skipped on a  
      fresh install); /prof changelog reopens them  
    - Trainer skill levels for 32 Blacksmithing and 12 Mining recipes, and  
      more vendor-sold items, from in-game recordings  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Known + trainable filter, /prof debug, data for build 70170  
    - New "Known + trainable" filter: known recipes plus ones a trainer teaches  
      at the character's skill (including probable trainer recipes); leaves out  
      pattern-only recipes

- Window: dropdown filters, main professions, learn sources, coin icons  
    - Filter and profession pickers are dropdowns (menu system where available,

    - Default filter is Known only (#2)

- Rename addon to Profit  
    The TOC, saved variables (ProfitDB, ProfitCharDB), global frame names and  
    messages now use "Profit". /prof still works, and /profit replaces  
    /professions. import\_recorded.py reads Profit.lua, and still reads  
    Professions.lua from before the rename.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add window, character rankings, export, minimap button  
    - UI.lua: /prof opens a sortable, filterable recipe window with a detail  
      pane; clicking a known recipe opens it in the profession window.  
    - Rankings default to the character's professions (known + learnable),  
      colored by skill-up chance; grey recipes stay listed.  
    - Known.lua reads profession skill levels and can open recipes.  
    - /prof export gives a shareable string; import\_recorded.py reads it and  
      keeps fields the string lacks.  
    - Minimap.lua: draggable minimap button, /prof minimap to hide.  
    - Rename global frames and slash command to avoid clashing with  
      Blizzard's ProfessionsFrame.  
    - Vendor prices are per item (client BuyPrice is per vendor stack).  
    - Recipe sources are a list (trainer and item can both apply);  
      automatic recipes count as trainer at skill 1.  
    - New trainer and merchant recordings from Stormwind.

- Initial addon: recipe data, Auctionator pricing, trainer/merchant recording  
    - tools/build\_recipes.py builds recipe data from WoW Forever client DB2 tables  
      (via wago.tools): materials, output, tools, stations, skill ranges, and where  
      each recipe is learned. Writes export/recipes.json and the addon's Data/*.lua.  
    - Core.lua prices recipes with Auctionator (vendor materials at vendor price),  
      with /prof top and /prof  commands.  
    - Record.lua records trainer learn levels and merchant stock in game;

    - Known.lua tracks which recipes each character knows.
